criteria.label: Anger, irritation and upset reactivity
criteria.definition: Ease/frequency of getting angry, irritated, annoyed or upset, across contexts.
criteria.high_evidence: Readily or often gets angry/irritated/upset at ordinary events.
criteria.low_evidence: Seldom feels angry/irritated/upset and is not easily annoyed.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Upset may include non-anger distress and remains keyed; record the emotion instead of deleting it. Opposed subcontents require mixed/qualified grading. Null means absent/inapplicable evidence;0 requires actual mixed/balanced evidence.

criteria.label: Bad mood
criteria.definition: Frequency/persistence of a bad mood, including crossness or other unpleasant mood.
criteria.high_evidence: Reports often being in a bad mood or lingering in one.
criteria.low_evidence: Reports generally even/good mood and uncommon bad moods.
criteria.mixed_or_null: N3 overlap does not erase explicit keyed bad mood; a single sadness event alone does not establish frequency. Null means absent/inapplicable evidence;0 requires actual mixed/balanced evidence.

criteria.label: Temper and keeping cool
criteria.definition: Temper loss, sharp reactions and maintaining composure, distinct from whether anger is felt.
criteria.high_evidence: Loses temper or has an uncontrolled sharp flare.
criteria.low_evidence: Keeps composure under provocation, whether or not anger is felt.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Strong inner anger alone does not prove temper loss; a smile alone does not prove composure. Distinct feeling/conduct clauses can score separately. Null means absent/inapplicable evidence;0 requires actual mixed/balanced evidence.

criteria.label: Complaint tendency
criteria.definition: Frequency/inclination to voice dissatisfaction or gripe, independent of required anger.
criteria.high_evidence: Frequently complains, dwells verbally on dissatisfaction or readily voices grievances.
criteria.low_evidence: Rarely complains or habitually leaves dissatisfaction unvoiced.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Constructive complaints can count when tendency is explicit. A bare factual correction alone is ambiguous; no anger prerequisite. Null means absent/inapplicable evidence;0 requires actual mixed/balanced evidence.

boundary_controls.definition: Hostility, anger, contempt, indifference and disregard for obligations can be valid facet evidence. quality.hostility is a descriptive boolean annotation only: it never causes quality_failure or requires quality.evidence. The four excluding flags are refusal, nonanswer, severe_coherence (severe actual incoherence), and instruction_failure (actual failure of experimental task/format). Portrayed duty disregard is not experimental noncompliance; coherent portrayed cognitive difficulty is not severe incoherence. Each true excluding flag needs literal quality evidence. Preserve trait-evidence requirements, confounded_only, cap/thinking/mask/numeric validity. Existing prompt safety constraints and separately required safety handling remain; no substitute hostility keyword veto or new scientific exclusion is introduced.
One-off access/role/ability constraints alone are ambiguous, not a blanket exclusion of explicit target habits.
Angry feeling, temper/composure and complaint differ; use distinct clauses. Broad upset/bad mood remains keyed.
Explicit complaint tendency can count without angry feeling, including constructive dissatisfaction.

evidence_allocation_policy: Allocate each exact passage to its best-fitting substantive primary dimension; overlapping slots remain null unless a genuinely distinct clause or evidence supports them. Within-dimension item subcontents share one grade. Contradictory subcontents require explicit mixed/qualified interpretation. These are guidance and diagnostics, not new eligibility/invalidation gates.

scorer: One blind once-lock scorer; identity recorded by common protocol; no author scoring of new model answers or extra execution rater.
statement_key: Expression grades direct, never reversed by statement direction; category alone insufficient.
